newsitem.title: UK: Dealers say Russian palladium exports in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dealers say Russian palladium exports in Tokyo.

text.p: Precious metals dealers here confirmed on Thursday that exports palladium from Russia have begun to arrive in Tokyo.
Platinum shipments are due next week, one source said.
Administrative snags delayed until now 1997 shipments from Russia to Japan the world's biggest importer of platinum group metals.
Russia is the largest exporter of palladium and the second biggest platinum shipper after South Africa.
"We have received our shipments," a dealer working at the London arm of a major Japanese trading conglomerate said, adding that the quantity was pro rata against the company's long term contract.
He believed other trading houses had also received metal from Almazjuvilirexport, the Russian platinum and palladium export agency.
"Some shipments have arrived," another dealer said.

Palladium was priced at $166.00/$170.00 and platinum at $396.00/$400.00 on Thursday off high fixes struck last month of $240.00 and $495.00 repectively when the absence of Russian material sent prices soaring to their highest levels in seven years and 17 years respectively.
"Themarket is still very tight and it is unlikely to return to normal this year," a dealer said.
However he forecast palladium prices would have to come off further before consumers were tempted to build up stocks which had been depleted during Russia's near seven month absence from the market.
"At $150 and below I would be a scale down buyer," he said.
Platinum prices were unlikely to fall as much as palladium when the Russians begin exporting that metal, dealers said.
They estimated a fall to around $370.00 per ounce, roughly the level seen at the beginning of the year as the floor for platinum.
Palladium prices began the year around $120.00 but dealers forecast a fall to around $130.00 as normality returned.
The presence of a huge inventory of palladium being held by the Tiger Management fund hanging over the market would put pressure palladium prices, one dealer said.
He noted that the rising liquidity and easier palladium prices this week probably resulted from Tiger Management selling small parcels into the dealer market.
Borrowing rates for both metals were still much higher than usual at 20-60 percent compared with 3-5 percent for a month routinely.
"Dealers are quoting tentatively and rates are negiotiable," a dealer said.
